proposal.title: Remote assistance from GenroApp, with code shared with the Meetlot desktop app
proposal.author: Giovanni Porcari

problem.p: A GenroApp user who needs help has the menu item "Richiedi assistenza…". It opens https://meetlot.genro.com/support. That page does not exist on the Meetlot server.

The remote control of a Mac, the sign-in through the system browser and the Developer ID signing exist today only inside the Meetlot desktop app. GenroApp needs the first and the third, and could need the second. Copying them into GenroApp gives two copies to keep aligned.
Signing and notarization are a Softwell process for every app of team HXS58UUB2N. Today they are written as Meetlot scripts, with Meetlot names and a personal notarytool profile.

section.title: GenroApp
section.fact: The menu has a "Meetlot" submenu with "Riunioni di team" and an "Assistenza" submenu with "Richiedi assistenza…". This code is in the working tree, not committed.
"Riunioni di team" opens https://meetlot.genro.com/call in a window; "Richiedi assistenza…" opens https://meetlot.genro.com/support with app=<name of the active document>.
Both windows are plain webviews: no initialization script, no native command granted.
Bundle id it.softwell.genropy.runner.
The app runs a Python sidecar named genropy-sidecar, a second executable to sign inside the bundle.
The app is signed ad hoc. The decision "How is the macOS app notarized?" is open, between an Apple ID with app-specific password and an App Store Connect API key.

section.title: Meetlot desktop app (kajenn-webrtc/desktop)
section.fact: Remote control state: one grant per app with lease, window, target process and window id. It ends on stop, on a heartbeat older than 9 seconds, after 30 minutes, on navigation and when the window closes.
The native commands accept only a page whose origin is https://meetlot.genro.com and whose path is /call.
The native consent panel is an NSAlert that names the controller and lets the user choose the controllable window.
The page adapter runs only in the top frame of https://meetlot.genro.com/call.
The control log is written in ~/Library/Logs/Meetlot/controllo.log.
The system-browser sign-in has the Keycloak realm softwell, the client id meetlot and the Meetlot callback written as constants.
The release script has the team, the bundle id it.softwell.meetlot, the sidecar name meetlot-assist and the camera and microphone entitlements written in it.
The provisioning-profile script builds an empty Xcode project whose only Meetlot-specific values are the bundle id and the entitlements file.
Notarization runs by hand with the keychain profile gp-notary-tool, an Apple ID with an app-specific password.
section.p: The proposal "Full-screen remote control in the Meetlot desktop app" (kajenn-webrtc/xmldocs/proposal/meetlot-full-screen-control.xml, not committed yet) replaces the Accessibility actions with real CGEventPost events, allows control only on a whole shared display, adds the controller zoom and the local-user pause.

section.title: Meetlot server (kajenn-webrtc)
section.fact: The server has rules for /admin and /call only. No page, asset or route answers /support.
A room is created from a description: room id, administrator and guest invitations valid 7 days. The LiveKit room is created when the administrator joins.
RtcRooms.create_room passes only the name and the metadata to CreateRoomRequest: no participant limit.
The LiveKit API used by the project accepts max_participants, empty_timeout and departure_timeout in CreateRoomRequest.

section.title: Apple tooling
section.fact: notarytool accepts an App Store Connect API key with --key, --key-id and --issuer, also in store-credentials.

section.title: 1. Shared code: one Tauri plugin crate
section.p: The shared desktop code moves into one Rust crate, a Tauri 2 plugin. The crate has no name yet. Both apps depend on it by git tag.

row.cell: The CGEventPost version of the full-screen control proposal, built by the crate's build.rs.
Same panel, text "control covers the whole screen", display choice on several displays.
Same rules; the commands support_start and support_event become plugin commands.
Initialization script that the plugin adds to the windows the app names.
Same file format; the directory comes from the app name.
Global shortcut registered by the plugin.
Same flow; Keycloak endpoint, client id and server callback passed by the app.

section.p: Each app gives the plugin its own configuration:

list.item: the trusted pages: origin and paths (Meetlot: /call; GenroApp: /support);
the window labels that receive the page adapter;
the Keycloak client and callback, only for an app that uses the sign-in.

rule.why: A page outside the list could otherwise ask for control of the Mac.

section.rule: The plugin refuses the native commands from any page outside the trusted pages of the app.
section.p: Each app keeps its own windows, menus, bundle id, Info.plist strings and sidecar.

section.title: 2. Signing and notarization as a Softwell process
section.p: One set of scripts and one booklet serve every macOS app of team HXS58UUB2N. They take the app-specific values as input:

list.item: bundle id;
path of the built .app;
entitlements file;
nested executables to sign first, each with its identifier (Meetlot: meetlot-assist; GenroApp: genropy-sidecar).

section.p: The scripts do, in order: Developer ID provisioning profile through the empty Xcode project, signing with hardened runtime and timestamp, notarization of the zip, staple, rebuild of the zip, dmg signed and notarized, verification with spctl and stapler validate.
Notarization uses a team App Store Connect API key, not a personal Apple ID:

list.item: Only the Account Holder can request API access in App Store Connect. Until then the personal profile gp-notary-tool stays in use.
The .p8 key, its key id and the issuer id are kept in 1Password, vault "Comuni Softwell".
On each build Mac, notarytool store-credentials saves them in the keychain under one profile name agreed by the team.
The updater private key of each app also lives in that vault, one key per app.

rule.why: It gives access to the notary service of the team.

section.rule: Write the API key, its ids or an updater private key in a repository.
section.p: The Meetlot booklet "Release Meetlot for macOS" becomes the Softwell booklet; Meetlot and GenroApp keep only their inputs.

section.title: 3. The assistance flow

diagram.title: A request for assistance from GenroApp

section.diagram: sequenceDiagram participant C as Customer (GenroApp) participant S as Meetlot server /support participant O as Operator participant L as LiveKit C->>S: open /support?app=NAME S->>S: record the request, create room id S->>L: create room, max_participants 2 S-->>C: waiting page, joined to the room S-->>O: new request in the operator list, notification O->>S: take the request S-->>O: token for the room O->>L: join C->>L: share the whole display O->>C: ask for control C->>C: native consent panel O->>C: real input events O->>S: close the request S->>L: end room

section.title: What /support does for the customer

list.item: Shows a form: the customer's name and one line on the problem. app from the query prefills the application name.
On submit, records the request and creates a dedicated room on the fly: LiveKit room with max_participants 2 and a short empty_timeout.
Joins the customer to the room and shows "waiting for an operator", with the position in the queue.
When the operator joins, offers one action: share the whole display.
When the operator asks for control, the native consent panel of the plugin opens.
Leaving the page, or the end of the request, ends sharing and control.

section.p: The page offers no room list, no invitations, no chat history, no recording.

list.item: An operator is a signed-in user with a dedicated tag. Without the tag the page shows the customer view.
The operator view lists the open requests live: time, customer name, application, problem line, state (waiting, taken, closed).
A new request raises a notification to every operator whose list is open.
"Take" assigns the request to the first operator who presses it; the others see it as taken.
The operator joins the room and has the remote control of the full-screen control proposal, zoom included.
"Close" ends the room and marks the request closed.

rule.why: A third person cannot enter an assistance session.

section.rule: The support room admits at most 2 participants; LiveKit enforces it with max_participants.

rule.why: Control covers the whole screen of the customer.

section.rule: Control in the support room needs the native consent of the customer at each request, as in Meetlot.
section.p: The server side needs a participant limit in RtcRooms.create_room (gramlot-webrtc) and the request list in kajenn-webrtc. The minimal client side is the /support page plus the plugin in GenroApp; GenroApp does not include the rest of Meetlot.

decision.question: Where does the shared crate live?

option.title: Its own repository, both apps depend on a git tag
Inside kajenn-webrtc/desktop, GenroApp depends on a git path of that repository
Inside genroapp, Meetlot depends on it

decision.question: If it has its own repository, under which GitHub organisation? GenroApp is in genropy, Meetlot in kajenn-org.
Does the crate start from today's Accessibility control or after the full-screen control proposal is implemented in Meetlot?

option.title: After: the crate starts from CGEventPost
Before: extract now, change inside the crate

decision.question: Where do the Softwell signing scripts and booklet live?

option.title: In the repository of the shared crate
In a repository of their own

decision.question: Which keychain profile name do build Macs use for the team API key?
How does /support know who the customer is?

option.title: Name typed in the form, no sign-in
Request signed by the GenroPy instance the customer works in
Keycloak sign-in through the system browser

decision.question: Who may open a request? Without a limit any browser can create rooms on /support.
Which identity tag marks a support operator?
How is an operator with no open list notified?

option.title: Only operators with the list open
Also a notification of the Meetlot desktop app

decision.question: Where are the requests kept? In memory they are lost at an update of the pod.

option.title: In the application instance, part of the update snapshot
In a database table, with history

decision.question: Does GenroApp keep the "Riunioni di team" item that opens /call?

option.title: Remove it: full meetings belong to the Meetlot app
Keep it as a plain web window, without control

list.item: Remote control and its consent rules exist once, for both apps.
A change to the native input reaches GenroApp with a tag update.
Any Softwell macOS app is signed and notarized with the same scripts and the team key.
Notarization no longer depends on one person's Apple ID once the team API key exists.
gramlot-webrtc gains a participant limit; kajenn-webrtc gains the /support page and the request list.
GenroApp needs Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions on the customer's Mac, asked at the first assistance.
Windows and Linux need their own native input code; this proposal covers macOS.
